mechanism_narrative: Four consecutive weeks of rising WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicate a sustained return to in-person work routines, which mechanically raises incidental retail and recreation visits (commute-adjacent shopping, lunch trips) over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -38.6 to -28.9 over four weeks
fact:TRANSIT rose from -56.9 to -48.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their upward trend for at least two more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below a sustained threshold (indicating reduced stay-at-home compliance consistent with eased restrictions), retail and recreation mobility will rise over the following four weeks as discretionary movement resumes.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 14 points above baseline and continues declining week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 17.9 to 13.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even after RESIDENTIAL falls below the 14-point threshold for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES creates a compounding behavioral effect: commuters who resume transit use and office attendance simultaneously increase discretionary retail stops, producing a larger RETAIL_REC gain than either series alone would predict over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by more than 3 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.6 points and WORKPLACES improved 4.1 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC gain over the next two weeks is no larger than the gain predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, measured via regression residual comparison.

mechanism_narrative: The non-monotonic swing in PARKS (sharp drop at t-2w followed by partial recovery) suggests transient weather-driven substitution between outdoor and indoor leisure; as weather stabilizes, suppressed outdoor demand shifts back toward indoor retail and recreation venues within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -26.4 to -36.6 then recovered to -27.1 and -28.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS rebound, or moves in the opposite direction of PARKS changes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week normalization in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -10.6 to -3.3 to -0.9) signals broader consumer comfort with in-person errands, which typically precedes similar normalization in less essential retail and recreation activity within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -10.6 at t-2w to -0.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show a comparable acceleration in its rate of improvement within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM nearing baseline (within 2 points of 0).

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT crosses above -45 points (a threshold historically associated with relaxed transit capacity limits), it signals a formal policy shift toward reopening that will drive sustained retail recovery over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 points relative to baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT currently at -48.7, approaching the -45 threshold after rising from -56.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth stalls or reverses in the four weeks after TRANSIT crosses -45, despite the threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: Continuous week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects a steady behavioral shift away from home-centric routines, which directly correlates with increased short-horizon retail and recreation visits the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week from 17.9 to 13.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL decline, observed in a majority of recent weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week RETAIL_REC gains are shrinking (6.6, then 0.3, then 6.6, then 3.1 points), and this deceleration, combined with volatile PARKS behavior, signals approaching saturation of the recovery trend; absent a renewed trigger from WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, RETAIL_REC growth will flatten or reverse over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: weekly RETAIL_REC delta falls below 2 points for two consecutive weeks while PARKS remains volatile
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains shrank from 6.6 to 3.1 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at an accelerating or stable rate over the next four weeks despite shrinking weekly deltas and PARKS volatility.
